items.name: The First Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt have no other gods.
items.explanation: We should fear, love, and trust in God above all things.

questions.title: Fear, Love, and Trust in God
The One True God of All Nations

reflection.prompt: Luther says we should fear, love, and trust in God above all things. What is one thing you love a lot?
What does it mean to trust someone? Who do you trust to take care of you?
Luther does not say only 'do not bow to idols' -- he says fear, love, and trust God ABOVE ALL THINGS. How could a good thing (a friendship, a sport, a phone) become a god?
Why do you think Luther puts fear first, before love and trust?
If the First Commandment claims the heart and not merely the hands, can anyone keep it? Where does that drive us?

items.name: The Second Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord, thy God, in vain.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not curse, swear, use witchcraft, lie, or deceive by His name, but call upon it in every trouble, pray, praise, and give thanks.

questions.title: Salvation in the Name of Jesus
Calling on the Name of the Lord
Misusing God's Name: Cursing and Sorcery
False Swearing and Lying by God's Name
Praise the Name of the LORD

reflection.prompt: What is your name? How does it feel when someone uses your name to be mean?
Luther says we should call on God's name when we are in trouble. Name one time you could pray.
This commandment has a 'not' half and a 'but' half. Why is avoiding bad words not enough?
What is the difference between using God's name and using it in vain?
Luther lists cursing, swearing, witchcraft, lying, and deceiving by God's name together. What do those five share?

items.name: The Third Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt sanctify the holy-day.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not despise preaching and His Word, but hold it sacred, and gladly hear and learn it.

reflection.prompt: What do we do at church that helps us learn God's Word?
Luther says we should GLADLY hear God's Word. What does gladly mean?
Notice that Luther does not mention resting, or a particular day of the week. What does he say the day is FOR?
How could someone sit in church every Sunday and still despise preaching?
Why does Luther define keeping the holy day around the Word rather than around rest?

items.name: The Fourth Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt honor thy father and thy mother.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not despise nor anger our parents and masters, but give them honor, serve, obey, and hold them in love and esteem.

questions.title: The Wise Son Honors His Parents

reflection.prompt: Name one way you could help at home this week.
What is the difference between obeying right away and obeying slowly?
Luther includes 'masters' -- teachers, employers, authorities. Why would God attach honor to an office and not only to a person you like?
Honor is more than obedience. What do you still owe a parent you disagree with?
This is the first commandment with a promise attached. What does it mean that God ties earthly blessing to the honoring of parents?

items.name: The Fifth Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt not kill.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not hurt nor harm our neighbor in his body, but help and befriend him in every bodily need.

questions.title: My Times Are in God's Hands

reflection.prompt: Who is someone you could be kind to today?
Luther says we should help our neighbor when he is hurt. What could you do if a friend fell down?
Luther turns 'thou shalt not kill' into 'help and befriend him in every bodily need.' Why is leaving someone alone not enough?
What does it mean to harm someone in his body without ever touching him?
How does this commandment reach both the anger in the heart and the neighbor's bodily needs -- food, shelter, safety?

items.name: The Sixth Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt not commit adultery.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may lead a chaste and decent life in words and deeds, and each love and honor his spouse.

questions.title: Male and Female He Created Them

reflection.prompt: Why is it good that families love each other?
Luther says we should be decent in our words. What kind of words are not decent?
Luther says 'in words and deeds.' Why does he include words?
What does it mean to honor someone else's marriage?
Luther frames purity positively -- leading a chaste and decent life, and loving and honoring one's spouse. How does that reframe chastity for married and unmarried alike?

items.name: The Seventh Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt not steal.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not take our neighbor's money or property, nor get them by false ware or dealing, but help him to improve and protect his property and business.

reflection.prompt: What does it mean to take something that is not yours?
Luther says we should help our neighbor keep his things safe. How could you do that?
'False ware or dealing' means cheating in business. How is cheating a customer the same sin as stealing from him?
Why does Luther say we should help our neighbor IMPROVE his property, not merely leave it alone?
What does the Seventh Commandment ask of an employer, a seller, and a borrower?

items.name: The Eighth Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not deceitfully belie, betray, slander, or defame our neighbor, but defend him, speak well of him, and put the best construction on everything.

questions.title: Love Covers and Believes the Best

reflection.prompt: What is a lie? Why does it hurt?
Luther says we should speak well of our neighbor. Who could you say something good about?
'Put the best construction on everything' means assuming the kindest explanation. When is that hardest?
Is it possible to break this commandment by repeating something that is true?
Luther requires defending the neighbor's reputation, not merely avoiding lies. What does that demand in an age of instant sharing?

items.name: The Ninth Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not craftily seek to get our neighbor's inheritance or house, and obtain it by a show of right, etc., but help and be of service to him in keeping it.

reflection.prompt: What does it mean to want something that belongs to someone else?
Luther says we should help our neighbor keep what is his. What would helping look like?
This commandment names a sin that can be perfectly legal -- getting a thing 'by a show of right.' How can something be lawful and still be sin?
Why do you think God gives a commandment about wanting, and not only about doing?
The Ninth and Tenth Commandments govern desire itself. What does that reveal about where sin actually begins?

items.name: The Tenth Commandment
items.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife, nor his man servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his cattle, nor anything that is his.
items.explanation: We should fear and love God that we may not estrange, force, or entice away our neighbor's wife, servants, or cattle, but urge them to stay and do their duty.

reflection.prompt: Have you ever wanted a friend to like you more than someone else? What did you do?
Luther says we should help people do their duty. What is one of your duties?
This commandment is about drawing people away from where they belong. How does that happen today?
Why does Luther say we should urge them to STAY?
How do the Ninth and Tenth Commandments together guard a neighbor's whole household -- his property and his relationships?

items.name: What Does God Say of All These Commandments?
items.text: I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate Me, and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love Me and keep My commandments.
items.explanation: God threatens to punish all that transgress these commandments. Therefore we should dread His wrath and not act contrary to these commandments. But He promises grace and every blessing to all that keep these commandments. Therefore we should also love and trust in Him, and gladly do according to His commandments.
items.ref_note: Luther's own text cites '[Exod. 20, 5 f.]' inline before the quoted Law; 'f.' (following) read as covering v.6, matching the quoted wording through 'and shewing mercy... keep my commandments.'

questions.title: Seek the Lord While He May Be Found

reflection.prompt: God says He shows mercy. What does mercy mean?
What does God promise to those who love Him and keep His commandments?
This close carries both a threat and a promise. Which do you notice first, and why?
Why would God attach a warning AND a blessing to the same commandments?
Luther says we should dread God's wrath and also love and trust Him. How do those two live together in one heart?

questions.title: The Law Written on the Heart
The Giving of the Ten Commandments
The Fruits of the Sinful Nature

items.name: The First Article — Of Creation
items.text: I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth.
items.explanation: I believe that God has made me and all creatures; that He has given me my body and soul, eyes, ears, and all my limbs, my reason, and all my senses, and still preserves them; in addition thereto, clothing and shoes, meat and drink, house and homestead, wife and children, fields, cattle, and all my goods; that He provides me richly and daily with all that I need to support this body and life, protects me from all danger, and guards me and preserves me from all evil; and all this out of pure, fatherly, divine goodness and mercy, without any merit or worthiness in me; for all which I owe it to Him to thank, praise, serve, and obey Him. This is most certainly true.

questions.title: Body and Soul Belong to God
Made in God's Image, Redeemed in Christ
Bless the Lord, O My Soul
A Life of Prayer and Praise

reflection.prompt: Luther says God gave you your body, your eyes, and your ears. Name one part of you that God made.
Who gives you your food and your clothes?
Luther says God STILL preserves all of this. What difference does the word 'still' make?
The article ends 'without any merit or worthiness in me.' Why does Luther add that?
If God gives daily bread even to the wicked, what is distinctive about a Christian's confession of creation?

items.name: The Second Article — Of Redemption
items.text: And in Jesus Christ, His only Son, our Lord; who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary; suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead, and buried; He descended into hell; the third day He rose again from the dead; He ascended into heaven, and sitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from thence He shall come to judge the quick and the dead.
items.explanation: I believe that Jesus Christ, true God, begotten of the Father from eternity, and also true man, born of the Virgin Mary, is my Lord, who has redeemed me, a lost and condemned creature, purchased and won me from all sins, from death, and from the power of the devil, not with gold or silver, but with His holy, precious blood and with His innocent suffering and death, in order that I may be His own, and live under Him in His kingdom, and serve Him in everlasting righteousness, innocence, and blessedness, even as He is risen from the dead, lives and reigns to all eternity. This is most certainly true.

questions.title: Calling on the Name of the Lord
Born of Woman, Under the Law
Through Whom All Things Were Made
Not Ashamed to Call Us Brothers
Son of David, Son of Man
Born to Bear Witness to the Truth
My God, Why Have You Forsaken Me

reflection.prompt: Who is Jesus, according to the Creed?
Luther says Jesus has redeemed me -- bought me back. What does it mean to buy something back?
Luther says Christ purchased us 'not with gold or silver, but with His holy, precious blood.' Why make that comparison?
Luther calls himself 'a lost and condemned creature.' Why start there before speaking of redemption?
Christ redeemed us 'that I may be His own, and live under Him in His kingdom.' What, then, is redemption FOR?

items.name: The Third Article — Of Sanctification
items.text: I believe in the Holy Ghost; one holy Christian Church, the communion of saints; the forgiveness of sins; the resurrection of the body; and the life everlasting. Amen.
items.explanation: I believe that I cannot by my own reason or strength believe in Jesus Christ, my Lord, or come to Him; but the Holy Ghost has called me by the Gospel, enlightened me with His gifts, sanctified and kept me in the true faith; even as He calls, gathers, enlightens, and sanctifies the whole Christian Church on earth, and keeps it with Jesus Christ in the one true faith; in which Christian Church He forgives daily and richly all sins to me and all believers, and at the last day will raise up me and all the dead, and will give to me and to all believers in Christ everlasting life. This is most certainly true.

questions.title: A New Heart and Good Works
God Desires All to Be Saved
Teach Me to Do Your Will
The Life of the First Congregation
Christ the Head of the Body
One Lord, One Faith, One Baptism
Forgiveness Delivered by Word and Sacrament
That They May All Be One
The Gates of Hell Shall Not Prevail
The Lord Is My Light and My Salvation
A Resurrection of the Just and the Unjust
I Know That My Redeemer Lives
The Fire That Is Not Quenched
Fullness of Joy in His Presence
A New Heaven and a New Earth
Like a Thief in the Night
Appointed Once to Die, Then Judgment
The Resurrection at the Last Day
As the Deer Pants for the Water

reflection.prompt: Who helps us believe in Jesus?
Luther says the Holy Ghost gathers the whole Christian Church. What is the Church?
Luther says 'I cannot by my own reason or strength believe.' Why is that good news rather than bad news?
How does the Holy Ghost call, gather, enlighten, and sanctify?
Luther grounds faith itself in the Spirit's work. What does that say about assurance, and about how we evangelize?

questions.title: God Known in Creation and Conscience
The Work of the Triune God

items.name: The Introduction
items.text: Our Father who art in heaven.
items.explanation: God would thereby tenderly urge us to believe that He is our true Father, and that we are His true children, so that we may ask Him confidently, with all assurance, as dear children ask their dear father.

questions.title: The Father Who Runs to Meet Us
Our Help Is in the Name of the Lord
You Shall Worship the Lord Alone
My Chosen Portion and My Cup

reflection.prompt: What do you call your father? What does God let us call Him?
Luther says we may ask God the way dear children ask their dear father. What would you ask?
Why would God want us to pray confidently rather than nervously?
What changes about prayer if God is truly OUR Father and not only my Father?
Luther says God 'would thereby tenderly urge us to believe.' How does the address itself teach faith before a single request is made?

items.name: The First Petition
items.text: Hallowed be Thy name.
items.explanation:
God's name is indeed holy in itself; but we pray in this petition that it may become holy among us also.

When the Word of God is taught in its truth and purity, and we as the children of God also lead holy lives in accordance with it. To this end help us, dear Father in heaven. But he that teaches and lives otherwise than God's Word teaches profanes the name of God among us. From this preserve us, Heavenly Father.

questions.title: The Name Not to Be Misused
God Puts His Name Upon His People
God's Name Blasphemed Because of Us

reflection.prompt: What does the word 'holy' mean?
Luther says God's name is already holy in itself. So what are we asking for?
God's name is hallowed among us when His Word is taught in truth and purity AND we live holy lives. Why both?
How could someone dishonor God's name while teaching about God?
Luther says he that teaches and lives otherwise than God's Word teaches profanes the name of God among us. What weight does that put on teachers?

items.name: The Second Petition
items.text: Thy kingdom come.
items.explanation:
The kingdom of God comes indeed without our prayer, of itself; but we pray in this petition that it may come unto us also.

When our heavenly Father gives us His Holy Spirit, so that by His grace we believe His holy Word and lead a godly life here in time and yonder in eternity.

questions.title: My Kingdom Is Not of This World
A Kingdom Not Observed by Sight
Pray That the Word Speed Ahead
Delivered from Darkness, Ruled by Christ
He Did Not Leave Himself Without Witness
Rule in the Midst of Your Enemies

reflection.prompt: What is a kingdom? Who is the king?
Luther says God's kingdom comes when we believe His holy Word. What helps you believe?
If God's kingdom comes 'without our prayer, of itself,' why pray for it at all?
What does it mean for God's kingdom to come 'unto us also'?
Luther ties the kingdom to the gift of the Holy Spirit and a godly life 'here in time and yonder in eternity.' How does that shape Christian hope?

items.name: The Third Petition
items.text: Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
items.explanation:
The good and gracious will of God is done indeed without our prayer; but we pray in this petition that it may be done among us also.

When God breaks and hinders every evil counsel and will which would not let us hallow the name of God nor let His kingdom come, such as the will of the devil, the world, and our flesh; but strengthens and keeps us steadfast in His Word and in faith unto our end. This is His gracious and good will.

questions.title: Not as I Will, but as You Will
The Devil, the World, and Our Flesh
God Works All Things for Good
To Destroy the Works of the Devil
To Become and Remain His Child
Living as His Child, Bearing Witness
Resist the Devil and He Will Flee
Free, Yet Doing All to God's Glory
Serving in the Calling God Gives
The Law of the Lord Is Perfect

reflection.prompt: Name one thing you know God wants you to do.
Luther says God breaks every evil plan against us. Who protects you?
Luther names the devil, the world, and our flesh. Why include our own flesh?
What would it look like for God's will to be done on earth as it is in heaven?
Luther prays that God would 'break and hinder every evil counsel and will.' What does it mean to pray against our own will?

items.name: The Fourth Petition
items.text: Give us this day our daily bread.
items.explanation:
God gives daily bread, even without our prayer, to all wicked men; but we pray in this petition that He would lead us to know it, and to receive our daily bread with thanksgiving.

Everything that belongs to the support and wants of the body, such as meat, drink, clothing, shoes, house, homestead, field, cattle, money, goods, a pious spouse, pious children, pious servants, pious and faithful magistrates, good government, good weather, peace, health, discipline, honor, good friends, faithful neighbors, and the like.

questions.title: Why Spend for What Is Not Bread?
In Him We Live and Move
Working Quietly for Our Own Bread
Good Government and a Peaceful Life

reflection.prompt: Name three things you need every single day.
Who gives us our food?
Luther's list of daily bread includes house, home, good government, and good friends. Why so broad?
God gives daily bread even to all wicked men. So what are we actually asking for?
We pray 'that He would lead us to know it, and to receive our daily bread with thanksgiving.' What does that say about gratitude being the real petition?

items.name: The Fifth Petition
items.text: And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
items.explanation: We pray in this petition that our Father in heaven would not look upon our sins, nor deny such petitions on account of them; for we are worthy of none of the things for which we pray, neither have we deserved them; but that He would grant them all to us by grace; for we daily sin much, and indeed deserve nothing but punishment. So will we verily, on our part, also heartily forgive and also readily do good to those who sin against us.

questions.title: Have Mercy on Me, a Sinner
Blessed Is the One Whose Sin Is Covered
Love Keeps No Record of Wrongs
You Forgave the Iniquity of My Sin

reflection.prompt: What does it mean to forgive someone?
Is there someone you need to forgive this week?
Luther says we are 'worthy of none of the things for which we pray.' Why pray at all, then?
This petition ties our being forgiven to our forgiving. How do you understand that?
We ask God not to look upon our sins nor deny our petitions on account of them. How does grace rather than merit ground this whole prayer?

items.name: The Sixth Petition
items.text: And lead us not into temptation.
items.explanation: God, indeed, tempts no one; but we pray in this petition that God would guard and keep us, so that the devil, the world, and our flesh may not deceive us, nor seduce us into misbelief, despair, and other great shame and vice; and though we be assailed by them, that still we may finally overcome and gain the victory.

questions.title: The Tempter and Our Own Desire
God Tests, but Does Not Tempt
Under the Shadow of the Almighty

reflection.prompt: What is temptation? Name something that tempts you.
Who helps you when you want to do something wrong?
Luther says plainly that 'God tempts no one.' What, then, are we asking for?
Luther says that even when assailed we may 'finally overcome and gain the victory.' What does that promise you in a hard week?
Misbelief, despair, and other great shame and vice -- why does Luther name misbelief and despair FIRST?

items.name: The Seventh Petition
items.text: But deliver us from evil.
items.explanation: We pray in this petition, as in a summary, that our Father in heaven would deliver us from all manner of evil, of body and soul, property and honor, and at last, when our last hour shall come, grant us a blessed end, and graciously take us from this vale of tears to Himself into heaven.

questions.title: The Lord Will Keep You from All Evil
A Very Present Help in Trouble
Our Dwelling Place in All Generations

reflection.prompt: What does it mean to be rescued?
Luther says God will graciously take us to Himself into heaven. What do you look forward to?
Luther calls this petition 'a summary.' A summary of what?
Why does Luther include evil of 'property and honor,' not only of body and soul?
The petition ends at our last hour, asking for a blessed end. How does praying for a good death shape the living of a life?

items.name: Amen
items.text: Amen.
items.explanation: That I should be certain that these petitions are acceptable to our Father in heaven and heard; for He Himself has commanded us so to pray, and has promised that He will hear us. Amen, Amen; that is, Yea, yea, it shall be so.

questions.title: Yours Is the Kingdom, the Power, and the Glory
Far More Than We Ask or Think
He Hears the Prayer of the Righteous
The Lord Reigns; Holy Is He

reflection.prompt: What does the word 'Amen' mean?
Luther says Amen means 'Yea, yea, it shall be so.' Say it together.
Luther says we should be CERTAIN these petitions are heard. Where does that certainty come from?
Why does it matter that God Himself has commanded us so to pray?
Luther grounds assurance in God's command and promise rather than in our feelings. How does that steady a doubting heart?

questions.title: The Psalms Teach Us to Pray

items.name: What Is Baptism?
items.explanation: Baptism is not simple water only, but it is the water comprehended in God's command and connected with God's Word.
items.where_written: Christ, our Lord, says in the last chapter of Matthew: Go ye into all the world and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

questions.title: The Washing of Water with the Word
Where His Name Is, There He Blesses
The Lord Will Fulfill His Purpose for Me

reflection.prompt: Have you ever seen a baptism? What did you see?
Luther says Baptism is not simple water only. What is added to the water?
Why does Luther insist it is not 'simple water only'?
What does God's command have to do with whether Baptism is more than a bath?
Water comprehended in God's command and connected with God's Word -- where else does Scripture attach a promise to a physical sign?

items.name: What Does Baptism Give or Profit?
items.explanation_heading: What does Baptism give or profit?
items.explanation: It works forgiveness of sins, delivers from death and the devil, and gives eternal salvation to all who believe this, as the words and promises of God declare.
items.where_written: Christ, our Lord, says in the last chapter of Mark: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved, but he that believeth not shall be damned.

questions.title: Baptized for the Forgiveness of Sins
The Promise Is for You and Your Children
Born Again Through the Living Word
Heal Me, for I Have Sinned Against You

reflection.prompt: Name one gift Luther says Baptism gives.
What does it mean to be forgiven?
Luther says these gifts come 'to all who believe this.' What is the 'this' that is believed?
Baptism works forgiveness, delivers from death and the devil, and gives eternal salvation. Why list all three?
How can a past event -- your own baptism -- deliver present help against death and the devil?

items.name: How Can Water Do Such Great Things?
items.explanation_heading: How can water do such great things?
items.explanation: It is not the water indeed that does them, but the word of God which is in and with the water, and faith, which trusts such word of God in the water. For without the word of God the water is simple water and no baptism. But with the word of God it is a baptism, that is, a gracious water of life and a washing of regeneration in the Holy Ghost, as St. Paul says, Titus, chapter three: By the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Ghost, which He shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ, our Savior, that, being justified by His grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. This is a faithful saying.
items.ref_note: The Titus quotation is embedded inline in Luther's own explanation, not posed as a separate 'Where is this written?' question (unlike 'What Does Such Baptizing with Water Signify?' below) -- verses cited cover the full quoted wording through 'This is a faithful saying' (Titus 3:5-8).

questions.title: A New Creation, Heirs with Christ
An Appeal for a Good Conscience
Send Out Your Light and Your Truth

reflection.prompt: Is it the water that does the great things, or something else?
Luther says without God's word the water is simple water. What makes it different?
Luther names two things: the word of God in and with the water, and faith which trusts it. What does each one do?
Why would Luther take such care to say the water itself does not do it?
Titus 3 calls it 'a washing of regeneration.' How does Luther hold the physical sign and the Spirit's work together without collapsing either?

items.name: What Does Such Baptizing with Water Signify?
items.explanation_heading: What does such baptizing with water signify?
items.explanation: It signifies that the old Adam in us should, by daily contrition and repentance, be drowned and die with all sins and evil lusts, and, again, a new man daily come forth and arise, who shall live before God in righteousness and purity forever.
items.where_written: St. Paul says Romans, chapter 6: We are buried with Christ by Baptism into death, that, like as He was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

questions.title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God
The New Self Raised with Christ
He Drew Me Out of Many Waters

reflection.prompt: Luther says something happens DAILY, not only once. What word does he use?
What does it mean to be sorry for doing something wrong?
Who is 'the old Adam,' and why must he be drowned daily rather than once?
What does the new man do, according to Luther?
Baptism is a once-for-all event with a daily shape. How does that inform repentance across a whole Christian life?

items.name: What Is Confession?
items.explanation:
Confession embraces two parts: the one is, that we confess our sins; the other, that we receive absolution, or forgiveness, from the confessor, as from God Himself, and in no wise doubt, but firmly believe, that our sins are thereby forgiven before God in heaven.

Before God we should plead guilty of all sins, even of those which we do not know, as we do in the Lord's Prayer. But before the confessor we should confess those sins alone which we know and feel in our hearts. Here consider your station according to the Ten Commandments, whether you are a father, mother, son, daughter, master, mistress, a man-servant or maid-servant; whether you have been disobedient, unfaithful, slothful; whether you have grieved any one by words or deeds; whether you have stolen, neglected, or wasted aught, or done other injury.

questions.title: Confessing and Reconciling with One Another
I Have Sinned Against the LORD
Repent, That Your Sins May Be Blotted Out
If He Refuses to Listen to the Church
Go and Tell Him His Fault
He Drew Me Up from the Pit

reflection.prompt: What does it mean to say you are sorry?
Luther says we hear that our sins are forgiven. Who forgives them?
Luther says Confession embraces two parts. Which part is ours, and which is God's?
Before God we plead guilty of all sins; before the confessor we confess only those we know and feel. Why the difference?
Luther says to receive absolution 'as from God Himself, and in no wise doubt.' What is at stake in that certainty?

items.name: The Absolution
items.explanation_heading: What does the confessor say in absolving?
items.explanation: As thou believest, so be it done unto thee. And by the command of our Lord Jesus Christ I forgive thee thy sins, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Depart in peace.

questions.title: Forgiven on Earth, Forgiven in Heaven
As Far as the East Is from the West
How Shall They Preach Unless Sent?
Order and Gifts in the Church

reflection.prompt: What are the words that tell us we are forgiven?
The confessor ends with 'Depart in peace.' How would that feel to hear?
The confessor says 'I forgive thee thy sins.' By whose command does he say it?
Why is absolution spoken out loud to you rather than only thought or felt?
'As thou believest, so be it done unto thee.' How do the words of absolution and faith belong together without faith becoming the thing that earns it?

items.name: What Is the Sacrament of the Altar?
items.explanation_heading: What is the Sacrament of the Altar?
items.explanation: It is the true body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, under the bread and wine, for us Christians to eat and to drink, instituted by Christ Himself.
items.where_written: The holy Evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke, and St. Paul, write thus: Our Lord Jesus Christ, the same night in which He was betrayed, took bread: and when He had given thanks, He brake it, and gave it to His disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is My body, which is given for you. This do in remembrance of Me. After the same manner also He took the cup, when He had supped, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Take, drink ye all of it. This cup is the new testament in My blood, which is shed for you for the remission of sins. This do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of Me.
items.ref_note: The institution narrative is attributed by Luther to 'Matthew, Mark, Luke, and St. Paul' collectively (a harmonized quotation, not a verbatim single-Gospel excerpt); verses cited here are each account's own institution passage.

reflection.prompt: What do we eat and drink at the Lord's Supper?
Who started the Lord's Supper?
Luther says the true body and blood are 'under the bread and wine.' Why does he not say instead of the bread and wine?
Why does it matter that it was instituted by Christ Himself?
What does Luther's plain reading of the words of institution commit us to, and what does it refuse to explain away?

items.name: The Benefit of the Sacrament
items.explanation_heading: What is the benefit of such eating and drinking?
items.explanation: That is shown us in these words: Given, and shed for you, for the remission of sins; namely, that in the Sacrament forgiveness of sins, life, and salvation are given us through these words. For where there is forgiveness of sins, there is also life and salvation.

questions.title: Love One Another as I Have Loved You

reflection.prompt: Luther says we receive forgiveness. What else do we receive?
The words say 'for you.' Who is 'you'?
Luther says 'where there is forgiveness of sins, there is also life and salvation.' Why does the one bring the others?
Why does Luther point to the WORDS to explain the benefit?
How does 'given, and shed for you' turn a general atonement into a gift delivered to a particular person?

items.name: How Bodily Eating Can Do Such Great Things
items.explanation_heading: How can bodily eating and drinking do such great things?
items.explanation: It is not the eating and drinking, indeed, that does them, but the words which stand here, namely: Given, and shed for you, for the remission of sins. Which words are, beside the bodily eating and drinking, as the chief thing in the Sacrament; and he that believes these words has what they say and express, namely, the forgiveness of sins.

questions.title: You Prepare a Table Before Me

reflection.prompt: Is it the eating and drinking that does the great things, or the words?
What do the words say we receive?
Luther calls the words 'the chief thing in the Sacrament.' Why not the bread and wine?
What does it mean that 'he that believes these words has what they say and express'?
Compare this with How Can Water Do Such Great Things. Why does Luther answer the same way in both Sacraments?

items.name: Who Receives the Sacrament Worthily
items.explanation_heading: Who, then, receives such Sacrament worthily?
items.explanation: Fasting and bodily preparation is, indeed, a fine outward training; but he is truly worthy and well prepared who has faith in these words: Given, and shed for you, for the remission of sins. But he that does not believe these words, or doubts, is unworthy and unfit; for the words For you require altogether believing hearts.

reflection.prompt: What does it mean to be ready for something important?
Luther says the one who believes is truly ready. Believes what?
